safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce from SAP 1.8 days to 1.60 days

narrative: Material PL1__MC7BAB87 shows steady daily demand averaging 541 units with moderate variability (CV=0.34) and no detectable trend. Lead times are highly volatile (CV=1.09, mean=0.89 days), making transport variability the dominant driver of safety stock. The (r,Q) continuous review policy is appropriate given the regular demand pattern and frequent replenishments. The storage capacity constraint (2,707.8 units) is binding, capping the order quantity below the unconstrained EOQ of 1,987 units.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is steady and high-frequency (non-zero 99% of working days) with moderate CV=0.34, making a continuous review (r,Q) policy optimal. It triggers replenishment exactly when inventory hits the reorder point, providing precise control without the excess holding cost of periodic review systems.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity of 2,707.8 units is fully binding (99.9% utilised at peak). The EOQ was reduced from 1,987 to 1,798 units, increasing ordering frequency slightly and raising annual ordering cost by ~$200. Any safety stock increase (e.g., for higher service levels) would require either a storage expansion or an OQ reduction below MOQ.
research_insights.escalation_flag: MOQ (1,068) + safety_stock (909) = 1,977 units which is within the 2,707.8 unit capacity — no MOQ-capacity infeasibility. However, capacity is extremely tight; any demand spike or supplier delay could require an emergency order exceeding capacity.
